name: Shannon Entropy-Directed Hardware Centrality Assignment (SEDHCA)
description: For each logical qubit, computes the Shannon entropy of its interaction distribution — qubits that interact broadly (high entropy) need central physical locations for routing flexibility, while focused qubits (low entropy) tolerate peripheral placement. Matches this entropy ordering to physical qubits sorted by closeness centrality (inverse mean BFS distance). This is an information-theoretic approach to placement that has no precedent in quantum compilation literature.

name: Interaction-Frequency Weighted BFS Anchor Placement (IFWBAP)
description: Identifies the single most-interacting logical qubit (highest weighted degree in the interaction graph) and anchors it to the most globally-central physical qubit (lowest mean BFS distance to all others). Then expands outward via a dual BFS: each subsequent unplaced logical qubit — selected by maximum interaction weight to already-placed qubits — is placed on the unoccupied physical neighbor of the current placement that minimizes total weighted distance to its already-placed interaction partners. Remaining unplaced qubits fill remaining physical qubits by hardware degree order.

name: Temporal-Decay Front-Gate Interaction Anchoring (TDFGIA)
description: Weights each interaction between logical qubits by an exponential decay based on the gate's circuit position: interactions appearing at gate index `t` receive weight `exp(-t / τ)`. This produces a temporally-biased interaction graph that prioritizes the early, front-layer interactions — exactly the ones that determine SWAP cost before routing can react. The resulting weighted graph is then used for the IFWBAP anchor-and-expand placement strategy.

name: K-Core Decomposition Hierarchical Centrality Matching (KCDHCM)
description: Computes the k-core decomposition of both the logical interaction graph and the hardware graph. The k-core number of a node measures the maximum subgraph density it belongs to — a fundamentally richer centrality notion than degree alone. Matching logical qubits to physical qubits by their respective k-core ranks ensures that the densest interaction clusters land in the densest hardware regions.

name: Gate-Sequence Sliding Window Adjacent-Pair Greedy Seeding (GSWAPS)
description: Examines the first K 2-qubit gates in circuit order (the "seeding window") and greedily places each interacting pair of logical qubits on an adjacent pair of physical qubits, prioritizing physical adjacency. This ensures the first K critical interactions are already "hardware-executable" before routing begins, eliminating early SWAP costs entirely for those gates. Remaining qubits fill by hardware degree.
